=== FINDINGS FROM deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro ===
- .claude/scripts/check_in_status.py (and twin): `_complete_dispatch_run_listing`, approximately line 370-398 in the shipped diff, lines 386-405 in the twin diff | severity=high | confidence=[4]
  PROBLEM: The function captures `total_count` from page 1 only, then uses that captured value for the break condition (`len(runs_by_id) >= total_count`) and the final completeness check (`len(runs_by_id) < total_count`). If a new run is inserted between pages and pushes an existing run from the read pages onto an unread page, the distinct-ID count can reach the stale `total_count` while that existing run is silently missed.
  WHY: A PR's review dispatch that was already in the listing can be pushed to an unread page by newly inserted runs during the brief pagination window. The function would falsely report a complete listing with no matching run, allowing the checker to hand the PR to a fixer mid-review. This is the same class of defect as issue #5442, though with a much smaller window (seconds of API pagination vs being permanently invisible after 100 dispatches). The test `test_listing_with_duplicates_across_pages_is_complete` has total_count grow from 101 to 102 across pages where the extra run IS on page 2, so it exercises the benign case (growth lands on a read page) but not the harmful one (growth pushes a run past the read pages).
=== END FINDINGS FROM deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro ===

=== FINDINGS FROM minimax_minimax-m3 ===
- workflow-templates/.claude/scripts/check_in_status.py: `_complete_dispatch_run_listing`, lines 388-405 (twin) / 372-396 (shipped, still using the page-1 total) | severity=high | confidence=[3]
  PROBLEM: `_complete_dispatch_run_listing` captures `total_count` from the first page only and uses that captured value both for the break condition (`len(runs_by_id) >= total_count`) and for the post-loop "fewer distinct ids than total_count" guard. When the listing grows between the page-1 read and the page-2 read, the new run(s) sit at position 1 (GitHub orders runs newest-first) and are never present on any page we read, because page 1 was already in hand before the insertion. The break then fires on the page-1 total (or on `len(page_runs) < 100` once the listing grows past the original total), the post-loop check compares against the original total, and the function returns a "complete" result that omits the newly added run.
  WHY: The checker's purpose is "is this PR's review still running?" If the run for this PR is the one that lands at position 1 between page 1 and page 2, the function reports zero matching runs and the helper returns 0, so the §26 checker / catch-all sweep can hand the PR to a fixer while the review is still in flight. The shipped file's `test_incomplete_dispatch_listing_defers_the_hand_back["listing-shifted"]` only exercises a same-`total_count` shift; a growing listing (the realistic race during high-volume dispatch windows) is not covered by any test.
- workflow-templates/.claude/scripts/check_in_status.py: `_complete_dispatch_run_listing`, around line 384 (twin) / 378 (shipped) | severity=low | confidence=[3]
  PROBLEM: The absent-wrapper check couples to `gh api`'s error wording: `if wrapper_may_be_absent and page_number == 1 and "HTTP 404" in str(exc): return None`. If `gh` rewords its error output (e.g. drops the literal `HTTP 404` substring in favour of an HTTP code in a structured field, the way other `gh` invocations have evolved), a 404 on the wrapper's first read stops looking like the absent-wrapper case and the function raises `ReadError` on every hand-back for repos that lack one of the two wrappers, holding the §26 checker in `retry` indefinitely.
  WHY: A `gh` release that changes the 404 message string would silently flip behaviour for every consumer repo that lacks `internal-review.yml` (or `ai-review.yml`), causing repeated `retry` verdicts and (per `changelog.d/5442-page-checker-review-dispatch-runs.md`) §26 dead-man's-switch decay followed by a `/implement-plan-claude` block stage after three retries. A two-line check that explicitly pulls the status code from `ReadError`'s payload (or that probes the wrapper with `actions/workflows/<wrapper>` first) would be stable against wording changes; matching the substring of an external tool's error text is not.
=== END FINDINGS FROM minimax_minimax-m3 ===

  WHY: A review run can move from `pending` to `queued` or `in_progress` after those listings have been read but before the `pending` listing. The root checker then sees no active run and can hand the PR to a fixer while review is still running. The new lifecycle-order test also expects the root checker to use the new order.
- .claude/scripts/check_in_status.py: `_complete_dispatch_run_listing`, page loop and `total_count` handling | severity=high | confidence=[4]
  PROBLEM: The helper records `total_count` only from page 1 and does not validate later pages' counts.
  WHY: If a new active run is added after page 1 is read, pagination can shift and repeat a run across pages. The distinct-ID count can still reach the original `total_count`, so the helper returns a complete listing while missing the new run. If that run is this PR's review, the checker can hand the PR to a fixer during review.
